page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The system is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2684.89. However, multi-core performance is weak, scoring 2695.68 in stress-ng and 1813.0 in Geekbench, both placing in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score is poor, and memory bandwidth for read-only small blocks is limited to 125.99 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while complex workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing show poor performance in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for compute-bound tasks that do not require substantial memory capacity. The high vCPU-to-RAM ratio limits its suitability for memory-intensive operations, database hosting, or high-throughput web serving, as evidenced by its poor database operations and static web serving throughput benchmarks. This server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, and simple background utility scripts that can leverage its strong single-core performance without exhausting the limited 2.0 GB memory footprint.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 compute-focused server featuring 2 vCPUs and 2.0 GB of RAM, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It contains 1 physical core with 2 threads, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng, but reveal significant multi-core and memory bottlenecks, with multi-core Geekbench and memory bandwidth tests scoring in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Due to its low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per core, this instance is highly constrained for memory-intensive workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, and simple background utilities, but is poorly suited for database operations, software compilation, or high-throughput web serving.
